correctness.rationale: The logarithmic first integral differentiates to zero, and positive levels are compact regular ovals without stationary points. The original physical-time quadrant Jacobian provides the stated normalized finite-amplitude density. Rescaling near the two endpoints gives integrable beta kernels; splitting the integral at its midpoint controls the remote endpoint, giving weak convergence and period constants. In the inverse-log contrast regime, a uniform integrable [u(1-u)]^(-1/2) bound proves convergence to exponential tilt. Finite tests corroborate rather than prove the asymptotic limits.

value.rationale: The asymmetric cubic center is a canonical positive-parameter subfamily of the global-center classification; uniform original-time sampling is intrinsic to its periodic dynamics. Endpoint selection, two beta laws with different decay exponents, and the inverse-log critical crossover are natural exact quantitative invariants useful for high-energy orbit averages; they are not simply global-center existence or a symmetric parameter substitution.
